title: These Finland homes get free heat from bitcoin miners (as long as BTC stays above $70,000)
summary: Title: These Finland homes get free heat from bitcoin miners (as long as BTC stays above $70,000) URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/08/these-finland-homes-get-free-heat-from-bitcoin-miners-as-long-as-btc-stays-above-usd70-000 Published Time: 2026-11-08T12:55:59.737Z Markdown Content: Nov 8, 2026, 7:55 a.m. EST 6 min read Summary * SunBit, a Finnish company, has installed 30 systems that use heat from Bitcoin mining to warm buildings, with mining revenue potentially covering electricity costs. * The systems cost roughly $20,000 or more to install and use more electricity than heat pumps, making their financial advantage dependent on Bitcoin prices, power costs and mining competition. * Bitcoin’s expected 2028 halving will cut new coin rewards in half, potentially before homeowners recoup their investment, and is not included in SunBit’s payback calculations. A 180-square-meter house in icy Nokia, a small town in Finland that gave the once-popular phone maker its name, has fully disconnected from the district heating network and now heats its rooms with a bitcoin miner. The machine sits inside what [SunBit](https://www.sunbit.fi/en/cases), a Finnish company, sells as a Bitcoin Boiler. Every kilowatt-hour a mining computer draws comes out as heat. SunBit captures that heat in water at up to 60°C and pushes it through a building’s radiators and floor pipes the way an oil or gas boiler would. The boiler earns bitcoin the whole time it runs. Essentially, the idea is that if the bitcoin earned covers the electricity consumed, the homeowner effectively gets heat without an ongoing net energy bill. But the system costs roughly $20,000 or more to install, and its profitability depends on bitcoin's price, electricity costs and the amount of computing power competing for mining rewards. “The heating itself works regardless of the market, and only the payback time moves,” Suomi said.
